extraction.unitDescription: This unit is intended to impart knowledge on principles of crop and animal production as well as agricultural extension. The knowledge will enable the trainee to appreciate the sources of food raw materials and their post-harvest handling, thereby being more effective in food processing and preservation technology. General Objectives General Objectives At the end of the unit, the trainee should be able to: Apply the principles of growing crops and handling the produce. Apply principles of rearing animals and handling their produce. Control common crop and animal diseases. Apply the principles of agricultural extension service
extraction.learningOutcomes: SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (COMPETENCIES) By the end of this unit, the trainee should be able to: Apply principles of crop production including land preparation, planting, nursery management, and harvesting techniques. Analyze ecological factors (climate, soil, and environment) affecting crop performance and recommend suitable practices. Identify and control common crop and animal pests and diseases using appropriate, sustainable methods. Demonstrate animal husbandry practices in managing ruminants, poultry, pigs, fish, and bees for safe and quality production. Apply post-harvest handling and storage techniques to maintain quality and reduce food losses. COURSE CONTENT / WEEKLY BREAKDOWN COURSE CONTENT / WEEKLY BREAKDOWN Week

extraction.unitDescription: COURSE DESCRIPTION: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes on human nutrition. The trainee will be equipped with knowledge on the nature and composition of food utilization and deficiency symptoms of nutrients in the human body. COURSE OBJETIVES: At the end of this course the student is expected to: Explain terms used in human nutrition Demonstrate the comprehension of the functions, sources and composition of nutrients. Describe the food composition, classification and functions of nutrients Apply knowledge of foods and nutrition in calculating dietary requirements of individuals and/or groups Understand the digestion, absorption, metabolism and excretion of all nutrients.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Classify different foods. Identify sources of carbohydrates and classify them. Identify and compare quality of protein from different sources. Distinguish and identify types and forms of lipids. Describe the process digestion of various food nutrients. Establish the changes of different food stuffs in the human body. Have the ability to evaluate energy values of various foods. Identify water uptake and loss mechanisms

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to equip the trainee with skills, knowledge and attitudes for managing nutrition for vulnerable groups in the community. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this unit, the trainee should be able to : Apply nutrition principles in identifying vulnerable groups Develop interventions for nutrition vulnerable groups Identify and management emerging issues and trends in nutrition vulnerable groups Describe factors contributing to nutrition vulnerability for the different groups
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Identify the vulnerable groups in the community Initiate appropriate nutrition interventions for the vulnerable groups Manage emerging issues and trends relating to the vulnerable groups Highlight factors predisposing people to vulnerability
extraction.references: Nutrition and Vulnerable Groupshttps: llmdp:.com/ books/pdfview/book/13500 Amanda Devine & Tanya Lewlis (2019). Nutrition and Vulnerable Groups. Royal College of Nursing (2012). Nutrition for vulnerable groups ASSIGNMENT Discuss factors contributing to vulnerability among the elderly(20 marks). GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows: Continuous Assessment Test15% Class Assignment 5% Class Presentation 10% End Term Examination 70% TO TOTAL 100% GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS Attendance: It is expected that every student will be in class for lectures and also participate in all practical exercises. Attendance records will be kept and used to determine each person’s qualification to sit for the final examination. Any student who has a class attendance of less than 80% will not be eligible to sit for the final exam. In case of illness or other unavoidable cause of absence, the student must communicate as soon as possible with any of the instructors, indicating the reason for the absence. Academic Integrity: Violations of academic integrity, including dishonesty in assignments, examinations, or other academic performances are prohibited. You are not allowed to make copies of another person’s work and submit it as your own; that is plagiarism. All cases of academic dishonesty will be reported to the University Management for appropriate sanctions in accordance with the guidelines for handling students’ misconduct as spelt out in the Students’ Handbook. Assignments and Group Work: Students are expected to submit assignments as scheduled. Failure to submit an assignment as at when due will earn you zero for that assignment. Only under extenuating circumstances, for which a student has notified any of the instructors in advance, will late submission of assignments be permitted. Code of Conduct in Lecture Rooms and Laboratories: Students should turn off their cell phones during lectures. Students are prohibited from engaging in other activities (such as texting, watching videos, etc.) during lectures. Food and drinks are not permitted in the laboratories. week Lesson Topic

extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Identify the vulnerable groups in the community Initiate appropriate nutrition interventions for the vulnerable groups Manage emerging issues and trends relating to the vulnerable groups Highlight factors predisposing people to vulnerability

GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows: Continuous Assessment Test15% Class Assignment 5% Class Presentation 10% End Term Examination 70% TO TOTAL 100% GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS Attendance: It is expected that every student will be in class for lectures and also participate in all practical exercises. Attendance records will be kept and used to determine each person’s qualification to sit for the final examination. Any student who has a class attendance of less than 80% will not be eligible to sit for the final exam. In case of illness or other unavoidable cause of absence, the student must communicate as soon as possible with any of the instructors, indicating the reason for the absence. Academic Integrity: Violations of academic integrity, including dishonesty in assignments, examinations, or other academic performances are prohibited. You are not allowed to make copies of another person’s work and submit it as your own; that is plagiarism. All cases of academic dishonesty will be reported to the University Management for appropriate sanctions in accordance with the guidelines for handling students’ misconduct as spelt out in the Students’ Handbook. Assignments and Group Work: Students are expected to submit assignments as scheduled. Failure to submit an assignment as at when due will earn you zero for that assignment. Only under extenuating circumstances, for which a student has notified any of the instructors in advance, will late submission of assignments be permitted. Code of Conduct in Lecture Rooms and Laboratories: Students should turn off their cell phones during lectures. Students are prohibited from engaging in other activities (such as texting, watching videos, etc.) during lectures. Food and drinks are not permitted in the laboratories. week Lesson Topic

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to impart knowledge to the student on appropriate nutrition for patients with STI and HIV/ AIDS and their management. The trainee will be able to conduct nutrition assessment and plan nutrition care to a HIV patient both in the hospital and at home. The course also incorporates the policies and practices recommended by the Ministry of Health and World Health Organization in the management of the disease. COURSE OBJECTIVES To explain types of STIS their treatments and drug nutrient interactions Explain HIV/AIDS, modes of transmission, spread and the nutrient requirements for HIV infected patients. Be able to counsel HIV/AIDS patients using the 9 critical nutrition practices (CCNP`s) To carry out nutrition assessment to HIV/AIDS patients To explain drug nutrient interactions as well as be able to prepare a food drug plan. To manage malnutrition in an HIV infected client using the commonly used therapeutic foods. Know the Kenyan national nutrition guidelines: Nutrition $ HIV guidelines, baby friendly hospital initiative, Infant feeding policies. To explain PMTCT.

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes on human nutrition. The trainee will be equipped with knowledge on the nature and composition of food utilization and deficiency symptoms of nutrients in the human body. COURSE OBJETIVES: At the end of this course the student is expected to: Explain terms used in human nutrition Demonstrate the comprehension of the functions, sources and composition of nutrients. Describe the food composition, classification and functions of nutrients Apply knowledge of foods and nutrition in calculating dietary requirements of individuals and/or groups Understand the digestion, absorption, metabolism and excretion of all nutrients.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Classify different foods. Identify sources of carbohydrates and classify them. Identify and compare quality of protein from different sources. Distinguish and identify types and forms of lipids. Describe the process digestion of various food nutrients. Establish the changes of different food stuffs in the human body. Have the ability to evaluate energy values of various foods. Identify water uptake and loss mechanisms

Establish the changes of different food stuffs in the human body. Have the ability to evaluate energy values of various foods. Identify water uptake and loss mechanisms

extraction.virtualPath: Course_outlines.zip/Course outlines/Course Outlines/Course Outlines/Martin Wanjohi/FOOD SAFETY AND HYGIENE COURSE OUTLINE (1).docx
extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to equip the trainee with knowledge, skills and attitudes in handling food safety and ensure that it remains safe for consumption. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Acquire knowledge and skills required to handle food safely Demonstrate the ability to handle and store foods in hygienic environment Identify food borne illnesses and the associated hazards Carry out inspection of food facilities Demonstrate hygienic food handling procedures.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) 1. To handle foods safely. 2. To handle and store foods in hygienic environment. 3. Know the food borne illness and the hazards. 4. Conduct inspection of food facilities 5. Handle foods hygienically GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows:

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes of Biological Sciences necessary for progression in career in the field of nutrition and dietetics. COURSE OBJECTIVES By the end of this unit, the trainee should be able to: Analyze the anatomy and physiological process of living things. Develop a positive attitude towards diverse plant and animal life in their surroundings. Recognize the relationship between living things and their environment. Recognize emerging issues and trends in biology
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, (Knowledge based) The trainee should be able to analyze the anatomy and physiological process of human beings. The trainee should develop a positive attitude towards various plant and animal life in the surrounding environment. The trainee should have the ability to understand the correlation between living things and their environment. The trainee should have the knowledge on emerging issues and trends in biology. Develop a positive attitude towards diverse plant and animal life in their surroundings. Recognize the relationship between living things and their environment. Recognize emerging issues and trends in biology UNIT LEARNING OUTCOMES / COMPETENCIES Upon successful completion of this course, (Knowledge based) The trainee should be able to analyze the anatomy and physiological process of human beings. The trainee should develop a positive attitude towards various plant and animal life in the surrounding environment.

extraction.unitDescription: This UNIT is intended to enable the students to acquire knowledge, skills and attitude on the nutrition care process. The learner will be able to undertake nutrition activities of the nutrition care process inpatient management.
extraction.learningOutcomes: At the end of this UNIT the trainee should be able to: Demonstrate the role of a nutritionist in patient management Apply the importance of nutrition care process Undertake the activities of the nutrition care process Evaluate the response of patients and clients to nutrition care and modify accordingly. GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE UNIT This UNIT will be graded as follows:

topics.topic: Introduction to the nutrition care process
topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · - Define Terms · -Explain the relationship between disease and nutrition · -Explain the roles of health professionals in the nutrition care process · - Describe the steps of nutrition care process

By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · -Describe the importance of nutrition assessment · -Explain the sources of nutrition assessment data · -Describe the types of nutrition assessment data · - Identify areas that require critical thinking in nutrition assessment

By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · -Identify the sources of data and tools of nutrition diagnosis · - Describe the problem/diagnostic label · - Identify the etiology and contributing factors to diseases · - Identify the signs symptoms of diseases · - Describe documentation of nutrition diagnosis information

By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · - Describe the types of nutrition interventions. · - Describe the data sources in giving nutrition interventions · - Describe how planning of nutrition interventions is done · -Explain the implementation of nutrition interventions · - Describe areas requiring critical thinking in nutrition intervention · - Explain documentation of nutrition intervention data

By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · -Define Terms · -Describe collection and use of nutrition monitoring and evaluation data · - Describe how to monitor a patient’s progress · - Describe measuring and evaluation of outcomes of interventions · - Describe areas requiring critical thinking in monitoring and evaluation · - Explain documentation of nutrition monitoring and evaluation data · -Determine techniques for continuation of nutrition care

By the end of the lesson the trainee should be able to: · - Describe emerging trends in nutrition care process · - Explain challenges experienced fitting in the new trends · - Describe the coping strategies to the emerging trends

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to give the trainee an overview of the Kenyan law and how it relates to Nutrition and Dietetics. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Describe the general set-up of Kenya’s legal system. Note the legal implications in relation to nutrition and dietetics issues. Identify the correct defense for various offenses. Adhere to status that apply to nutrition and dietetics. Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Describe the general set-up of Kenya’s legal system. Note the legal implications in relation to nutrition and dietetics issues. Identify the correct defense for various offenses. Adhere to status that apply to nutrition and dietetics. Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment. GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows:

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to give the trainee an overview of the Kenyan law and how it relates to Nutrition and Dietetics. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Describe the general set-up of Kenya’s legal system. Note the legal implications in relation to nutrition and dietetics issues. Identify the correct defense for various offenses. Adhere to status that apply to nutrition and dietetics. Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Describe the general set-up of Kenya’s legal system. Note the legal implications in relation to nutrition and dietetics issues. Identify the correct defense for various offenses. Adhere to status that apply to nutrition and dietetics. Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment. GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows:

topics.coverage: Meaning of terms · Constitution as the supreme law of Kenya.
topics.learningOutcomes: Identify the meaning of terms · Discuss the various aspects of Kenyan constitution.

topics.learningOutcomes: . · Identify the organization of the judiciary · Explain the Magistrate court (subordinate court) · Identify the role of Kadhi Courts

topics.coverage: High court (superior court) · Court of appeal · Supreme court
topics.learningOutcomes: Define supreme court and explain its functions in relation to nutrition and dietetics · Define and explain functions of court of appeal in relation to nutrition and dietetics · Define and explain functions of Supreme Court in relation to nutrition and dietetics

topics.coverage: Definition · General defenses · Capacity in tort · Specific tort
topics.learningOutcomes: Define terms · Identify the general defenses. · Discuss the capacity in tort. · Identify the specific tort.

topics.coverage: Definition · Duties of an employer · Duties of employee
topics.learningOutcomes: Define terms · Identify the duties of an employer · Discuss the duties of an employee

topics.coverage: Terms imposed by statutes · Types of dismissal · Reasons for dismissal
topics.learningOutcomes: Identify the terms imposed by statutes. · Explain types of dismissal. · Discuss reasons for dismissal.

topics.coverage: Types of businesses
topics.learningOutcomes: Identify types of business

topics.coverage: Methods of acquiring business premises
topics.learningOutcomes: Discuss methods of acquiring business premises

topics.coverage: Dangerous Drugs Act · Provisions of food, drugs, and chemical substances Act · The Public Health Act · Poisonous Substance Act

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to give the trainee an overview of the Kenyan law and how it relates to Nutrition and Dietetics. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Describe the general set-up of Kenya’s legal system. Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment.

extraction.unitDescription: COURSE DESCRIPTION COURSE DESCRIPTION COURSE OBJECTIVES COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this UNIT the trainee should be able to: Establishing Patient Dietary Needs Drawing Individualized Feeding Care Plan Carrying Out Feeding Care Plan Interventions Conducting Continuous Dietary Monitoring.GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE
extraction.learningOutcomes: Methods Establish Patient Dietary Needs

topics.learningOutcomes: Explain the meaning and types of dietary needs. Identify and explain various dietary assessment tools. Describe common dietary needs related to specific health conditions. Explain different dietary preferences and requirements. Identify and explain different feeding routes and necessary resources. Explain the role of family in dietary needs and various assessment methods.

Define and differentiate types of individualized feeding care plans. Identify tools for feeding and create a grocery list for a feeding plan. Select appropriate recipes and prepare a menu. Understand comprehensive assessment methods for care plan development. Conduct client diet counseling effectively. Utilize appropriate feeding tools and consider client preferences during interventions.

topics.topic: Carry Out Feeding Care Plan Interventions
topics.learningOutcomes: Integrate cultural practices and adhere to safe food handling procedures. Prepare and carry out individualized meal feeding. Implement proper cleaning procedures for feeding tools and understand assessment criteria.

Define continuous dietary monitoring and its importance. Conduct reassessments based on the client's responses. Administer reinterventions and disseminate reports appropriately. Identify situations for appropriate referrals and utilize correct documentation formats. Prepare for and undergo final assessments for continuous dietary monitoring.
Reinforce understanding of patient dietary needs, developing care plans, implementing interventions, and monitoring.

Apply all learned competencies in a simulated comprehensive caregiving scenario. Develop problem-solving and critical thinking skills in unexpected dietary situations. Explore current trends and advanced concepts in dietary interventions.
Identify and rectify common mistakes. Perform a simulated practical assessment under exam conditions. Prepare for and undertake simulated oral and written assessments.
Demonstrate competence in all unit outcomes through a comprehensive practical assessment.
Demonstrate comprehensive understanding and verbal communication. Demonstrate theoretical knowledge and understanding through written responses.
Receive feedback on performance and discuss future learning or career paths.

COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student is expected to: comprehend the principles of nutrition establish the nutritional requirements in different physiological stages. understand the types and causes of malnutrition. identify food security, types of food insecurity, and dimensions of food security. highlight the types of nutrition surveillance Understand the nutrition intervention programmes.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Understand the principles of nutrition Understand the nutritional requirements in different physiological stages. Identify the types of nutrition surveillance Understand the nutrition intervention programmes. G SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE

extraction.virtualPath: Course_outlines.zip/Course outlines/Course Outlines/Course Outlines/Martin Wanjohi/Entrepreneurship Education course outline -KNEC.docx
extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to equip the trainee with necessary knowledge, skills, values and attitudes that will enable him/her to plan, start, operate and manage a personal, group, private or public enterprise. It is also intended to instil in the trainee the drive necessary to venture into profit making activities.
extraction.learningOutcomes: By the end of this module unit, the trainee should be able to; - Appreciate the importance of entrepreneurship. Acquire entrepreneurial competencies necessary for planning, starting and managing a business Demonstrate positive attitude towards self-employment. Identify viable business opportunities Demonstrate entrepreneurial behavior in planning, starting and managing a business enterprise. Demonstrate creativity and innovation in their day to day business activities Appreciate the role of business planning Appreciate the emerging issues and trends related to the business environment. LEARNING OUTCOMES / COMPETENCIES

topics.coverage: Definition of terms · Differences between self and salaried employment · Contribution of entrepreneurship towards national development · EVOLUTION OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP · History of entrepreneurship in Kenya · Myths associated with entrepreneurship · Theories of entrepreneurship · Economic, political and social factors affecting entrepreneurial development
topics.learningOutcomes: This section is aimed at giving the student an overview of what entrepreneurship is all about. · It covers the introduction basics and evolution of entrepreneurship

topics.coverage: Types of entrepreneurs · Qualities/character traits of an entrepreneur · Role of an entrepreneur in an enterprise · Self-employment vs. Salaried employment
topics.learningOutcomes: Students will be taught on what to poses to be a successful entrepreneur

topics.coverage: Definition of terms · The process of creativity and innovation · Importance of creativity and innovation. · Barriers to creativity and innovation · Ways of managing barriers to creativity.
topics.learningOutcomes: Students are expected to understand how to analyse the entrepreneurial opportunities though creativity and innovation of available resources.

topics.coverage: The entrepreneurial culture. · Cultural habits that promote entrepreneurial development. · Factors inhibiting entrepreneurial development · ENTREPRENEURIAL OPPORTUNITIES · Meaning of business opportunity · Ways of generating ideas for business opportunities · Evaluation of business opportunities for viability
topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of this lesson the trainee should be able to: · Explain the concept of entrepreneurial culture. · Discuss habits that promote entrepreneurial development. · Discuss factors inhibiting entrepreneurial development. · Explain the meaning of business opportunity · Explain ways of generating ideas for business opportunities · Evaluation of business opportunities for viability

topics.coverage: Definition of entrepreneurial motivation · Entrepreneurial motivation factors · ENTREPRENEURIAL COMPETENCIES · Entrepreneurial competences in a business
topics.learningOutcomes: This lesson gives the learner a deeper understanding on the entrepreneurial motivational factors and competencies. · The learner is expected to identify the entrepreneurial motivation factors and explain the key entrepreneurial competencies in business

topics.coverage: Procedure of starting a business enterprise · Factors to be considered when starting a small enterprise · Forms of business ownership · Challenges faced when starting a small enterprise · The business life cycle · Support services available to small businesses
topics.learningOutcomes: This section is aimed at exposing student on how to start a business enterprise and identify the business support services available to a small business.
topics.activities: Lecture · Discussion with a · Resource person

topics.coverage: Definition of the term management · Functions of management in an enterprise · Methods of inventory management · Management of business resources
topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to: · Define and explain the functions of management in an enterprise · Explain the methods of inventory management · Explain the various methods of managing business resources

topics.coverage: Meaning of financial management Sources of business finance · Types of business records · Recording business transactions in the books of accounts · Preparation and interpretation of financial statements · Importance of budgeting to a business
topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to: · Explain the meaning of financial management · Explain the importance of financial management · Identify the various sources of business finance · Identify types of business records · Record business transactions in the books of accounts · Prepare financial statements · Interpret financial statements for business decisions · Explain the importance of budgeting to a business

topics.coverage: Definition of terms · Components of marketing · Process of Marketing · ENTERPRISE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY · Definition of terms · Meaning of enterprise social responsibility · Types of enterprise social responsibility · Importance of enterprise social responsibility · Ethical behaviour in a business enterprise
topics.learningOutcomes: Students will be expected to understand: · The components of marketing and ways of gathering market information · Identify the types of enterprise social responsibility and its importance · Establish the ethical behavior in a business enterprise

topics.coverage: Definition of business plan · Components of a business plan · Uses of a business plan
topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of this sub-module unit the trainee should be able to · Describe the components of a business plan · Explain the uses of a business plan · Prepare a business plan
topics.activities: Lecture · Case study · Write a business plan

topics.coverage: Definition of ICT · Benefits of ICT to a small enterprise · Uses of ICT equipment in a business enterprise · EMERGING ISSUES AND TRENDS · Definition of terms · Emerging issues and trends in enterprises management · Challenges posed by emerging trends in entrepreneurship.
topics.learningOutcomes: Students will be expected to understand the uses and benefits of ICT in a business enterprise and identify the current trends in entrepreneurship.

Develop an understanding of support and a sense of care and responsibility for disadvantaged groups in the community.

extraction.unitDescription: COURSE DESCRIPTION: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes on human nutrition. The trainee will be equipped with knowledge on the nature and composition of food utilization and deficiency symptoms of nutrients in the human body. COURSE OBJETIVES: At the end of this course the student is expected to: Explain terms used in human nutrition Demonstrate the comprehension of the functions, sources and composition of nutrients. Describe the food composition, classification and functions of nutrients Apply knowledge of foods and nutrition in calculating dietary requirements of individuals and/or groups Understand the digestion, absorption, metabolism and excretion of all nutrients.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Classify different foods. Identify sources of carbohydrates and classify them. Identify and compare quality of protein from different sources. Distinguish and identify types and forms of lipids. Describe the process digestion of various food nutrients. Establish the changes of different food stuffs in the human body. Have the ability to evaluate energy values of various foods. Identify water uptake and loss mechanisms

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes to perform effectively supervisory duties in an organization. extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes in nutrition through the lifespan. The trainer should have the ability to describe developmental milestones

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes in nutrition through the lifespan. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Understand terms used in nutrition throught the lifespan Appreciate the importance of nutrition throught the lifespan Acquire knowledge of health and nutrition problems affecting individual’s throught the lifespan. Understand factors influencing dietary intake of individual’s throught the lifespan. Appreciate the care process for the mother and the new born throughout the lifespan. Acquire knowledge on feeding throught the lifespan
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, (Knowledge based) The trainer should have the ability to explain the importance of nutrition in the lifespan The trainee should have the ability to identify the role and importance of MCH Services The trainee should have the ability to advice on pre-conception care and nutrition. The trainee should have the ability to advice on nutrition requirements during pregnancy The trainee should have the ability to provide nutrition care for the mother and the new born. The trainee should have the ability to provide nutrition care for infants between birth to 6 months. The trainee should have the ability to advice on complementary feeding. The trainer should have the ability to describe developmental milestones

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to impart knowledge to the student on appropriate nutrition for patients with STI and HIV/ AIDS and their management. The trainee will be able to conduct nutrition assessment and plan nutrition care to a HIV patient both in the hospital and at home. The course also incorporates the policies and practices recommended by the Ministry of Health and World Health Organization in the management of the disease. COURSE OBJECTIVES To explain types of STIS their treatments and drug nutrient interactions Explain HIV/AIDS, modes of transmission, spread and the nutrient requirements for HIV infected patients. Be able to counsel HIV/AIDS patients using the 9 critical nutrition practices (CCNP`s) To carry out nutrition assessment to HIV/AIDS patients To explain drug nutrient interactions as well as be able to prepare a food drug plan. To manage malnutrition in an HIV infected client using the commonly used therapeutic foods. Know the Kenyan national nutrition guidelines: Nutrition $ HIV guidelines, baby friendly hospital initiative, Infant feeding policies. To explain PMTCT.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Explain HIV/AIDS, modes of transmission, spread and the nutrient requirements for HIV infected patients. Be able to counsel HIV/AIDS patients using the 9 critical nutrition practices (CCNP`s)

extraction.virtualPath: Course_outlines.zip/Course outlines/Course Outlines/More course outlines/course outlines for September December Series/Lydia Wanja/course outlines/nutrition Intervention in HIVAIDS management.docx
extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to impart knowledge to the student on appropriate nutrition for patients with STI and HIV/ AIDS and their management. The trainee will be able to conduct nutrition assessment and plan nutrition care to a HIV patient both in the hospital and at home. The course also incorporates the policies and practices recommended by the Ministry of Health and World Health Organization in the management of the disease. COURSE OBJECTIVES To explain types of STIS their treatments and drug nutrient interactions Explain HIV/AIDS, modes of transmission, spread and the nutrient requirements for HIV infected patients. Be able to counsel HIV/AIDS patients using the 9 critical nutrition practices (CCNP`s) To carry out nutrition assessment to HIV/AIDS patients To explain drug nutrient interactions as well as be able to prepare a food drug plan. To manage malnutrition in an HIV infected client using the commonly used therapeutic foods. Know the Kenyan national nutrition guidelines: Nutrition $ HIV guidelines, baby friendly hospital initiative, Infant feeding policies. To explain PMTCT.
extraction.learningOutcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: (Knowledge based) Explain HIV/AIDS, modes of transmission, spread and the nutrient requirements for HIV infected patients. Be able to counsel HIV/AIDS patients using the 9 critical nutrition practices (CCNP`s)

extraction.unitDescription: This course is intended to equip learner with nutritional counselling skills for at-risk groups and individual, family and group levels, as well as knowledge of counselling techniques in cross-cultural and multi-cultural settings. COURSE OBJECTIVES To describe the scope of nutrition education and counselling To discuss factors that influence behavior To demonstrate counselling skills and techniques in health and nutrition To manage nutrition related complications To explain emerging issues and trends in health and nutrition education and promotion GRADING SYSTEM FOR THE COURSE This course will be graded as follows: Continuous Assessment Test15%
extraction.learningOutcomes: ACTIVITIES REMARKS Lesson1 Introduction to Nutrition Education and Counselling  Meaning of terms: nutrition education, counsellor, nutrition counselling  Origin and evolution of the field  Modern practices in nutrition: dietary guidelines, nutrition science, roles of professionals, public health initiatives  Objectives of nutrition education and counselling: healthy eating habits, improved dietary behaviors, empowerment, disease prevention  Principles of nutrition education: learner-centered, evidence-based, interactive, positive, culturally sensitive

topics.topic: Introduction to Nutrition Education and Counselling
topics.coverage:  Meaning of terms: nutrition education, counsellor, nutrition counselling ·  Origin and evolution of the field ·  Modern practices in nutrition: dietary guidelines, nutrition science, roles of professionals, public health initiatives ·  Objectives of nutrition education and counselling: healthy eating habits, improved dietary behaviors, empowerment, disease prevention ·  Principles of nutrition education: learner-centered, evidence-based, interactive, positive, culturally sensitive ·  Principles of nutrition counselling: client-centered, collaborative partnership, motivational interviewing, small changes, holistic approach
topics.learningOutcomes: This is intended to give an overview of the nutrition counselling

topics.coverage:  Meaning of healthy human behavior ·  Factors influencing behavior: personal, social, environmental, psychological ·  Health and nutrition education models and theories: Health Belief Model (HBM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), Social Cognitive Theory, Transtheoretical Model (Stages of Change Model), Social Ecological Model
topics.learningOutcomes: This is intended to give an overview of the nutrition counselling

Developing educational messages for individuals and groups: audience-specific, focus on benefits, clear language, realistic goals, motivational

extraction.unitName: Legal aspects in nutrition and dietetics.
extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes of Legal aspects in nutrition and dietetics, necessary for progression in career in the field of nutrition and dietetics.
extraction.learningOutcomes: By the end of this course unit, the trainee should be able to: Describe the general setup of Kenya legal system Know the legal implications in relation to nutrition and dietetics Identify the correct defences for various offenses Adhere to statutes that apply to nutrition and dietetics Adhere to legal requirements when operating a nutrition and dietetics establishment UNIT LEARNING OUTCOMES / COMPETENCIES By the end of this course/unit, the trainee should be able to: Describe the general structure and organization of the Kenya legal system. Explain the legal implications related to nutrition and dietetics practice.

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to provide the trainee with relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes in nutrition through the lifespan. COURSE OBJECTIVES At the end of this course the student should be able to: Understand terms used in nutrition through the lifespan Appreciate the importance of nutrition through the lifespan Acquire knowledge of health and nutrition problems affecting individuals through the lifespan. Understand factors influencing dietary intake of individuals through the lifespan. Appreciate the care process for the mother and the new born throughout the lifespan. Acquire knowledge on feeding through the lifespan

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · - Define housekeeping and its importance. - Identify different types of cleaning equipment. - Explain basic safety procedures in housekeeping.
topics.activities: - Introduce the course and learning outcomes. - Lecture on housekeeping roles and responsibilities. - Demonstrate safe handling of basic cleaning equipment. - Facilitate group discussion on safety protocols.
topics.assessment: Knowledge · 1. oral questioning · 2. written · Skills · 1. observation · 2. project · 3. portfolio · Attitudes · 1. observation · 2. third party reports · 3. external assessors
topics.resources: - Housekeeping Manual (e.g., Kenyan hospitality standards) - CDACC Occupational Standards for Housekeeping - Cleaning equipment samples (brushes, mops, buckets) - Safety data sheets (example)

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to --Categorize different cleaning materials. - Explain the proper use and storage of cleaning materials.
topics.activities: - Lecture on types of cleaning chemicals (detergents, disinfectants, abrasives). - Demonstrate proper dilution and application of cleaning agents. - Discuss safety precautions when handling chemicals.
topics.assessment: Knowledge · -Oral questioning on chemical classification. - Short written exercise on chemical safety rules. · Skills · 1. observation · 2. project · 3. portfolio · Attitudes · 1. observation · 2. third party reports · 3. external assessors
topics.resources: - Cleaning product labels (empty containers) - MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheets) examples - Short video on chemical handling.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to · - Demonstrate basic dusting and sweeping techniques. - Apply proper mopping procedures.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate correct dusting techniques for various surfaces. - Guide trainees through sweeping methods. - Demonstrate correct mopping techniques (two-bucket system). - Provide hands-on practice.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of dusting and sweeping (formative). - Trainer observation of mopping technique.
topics.resources: - Cleaning equipment (dust cloths, brooms, mops, buckets) - Sample work area (classroom floor, furniture) - Instructional videos on cleaning techniques.

topics.learningOutcomes: - By the end of the session trainee should be able to · -Perform spot cleaning and stain removal. - Clean different types of surfaces (glass, mirrors, wood).
topics.activities: - Demonstrate effective stain removal techniques for common stains. - Guide trainees on cleaning glass and mirrors without streaks. - Explain and demonstrate wood furniture care.
topics.assessment: - Practical assessment of stain removal (formative). - Observation of glass/mirror cleaning technique.
topics.resources: - Stain removal kits (various solutions) - Glass cleaner, wood polish, microfiber cloths - Samples of stained fabric, glass panels, wooden furniture.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to · - Understand the purpose of cleaning checklists. - Develop a basic cleaning checklist for a given area.
topics.activities: - Lecture on the importance of checklists for quality control. - Provide examples of different cleaning checklists. - Facilitate a group activity to design a checklist.
topics.assessment: - Group presentation and critique of designed checklists. - Oral questioning on the purpose of checklists.
topics.resources: - Sample cleaning checklists (hotel rooms, public areas). - Flip charts/whiteboard for group work.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Apply cleaning procedures to a designated public area. - Follow safety protocols during public area cleaning.
topics.activities: - Supervise trainees in cleaning a designated public area (e.g., hallway, reception). - Provide real-time feedback and correction. - Emphasize adherence to safety guidelines.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees clean a public area according to a checklist and safety standards (Summative for LO1). - Trainer observation and completion of a practical rubric.
topics.resources: - Designated public area for cleaning. - All necessary cleaning equipment and materials. - Safety signage.

topics.coverage: Understanding Beds and Beddings
topics.learningOutcomes: - Identify different types of beds and bed sizes. - Recognize various types of bed linen and their properties.
topics.activities: - Lecture on bed types (single, double, king, etc.) and their dimensions. - Display and explain different bed linen (sheets, duvets, pillows, blankets). - Discuss quality standards for beddings.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on bed types and bedding materials. - Short written identification quiz of bed linen.
topics.resources: - Visual aids of different bed types. - Samples of various bed linen (cotton, linen, microfiber). - Manufacturer's labels for bedding.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Prepare the guest room for bed making. - Gather necessary bed making supplies efficiently.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the sequence of preparing a room for bed making (e.g., stripping existing linen). - Guide trainees on organizing bed making trolleys/carts. - Emphasize hygiene practices.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of room preparation (formative). - Observation of supplies organization.
topics.resources: - Mock guest room setup (bed, bedside tables). - Clean and soiled linen hampers. - Bed making supplies (fresh linen, pillowcases).

topics.learningOutcomes: - Perform a basic occupied bed making procedure. - Perform a basic unoccupied bed making procedure.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate step-by-step the procedure for making an occupied bed. - Demonstrate step-by-step the procedure for making an unoccupied bed. - Provide hands-on guided practice for both.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of basic bed making (formative). - Trainer observation and feedback on technique.
topics.resources: - Guest room setup with a bed. - Full set of clean bed linen for each trainee/group. - Instructional diagrams/videos of bed making.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Make a hospital corner correctly. - Prepare different types of bed setups (e.g., turn-down service, extra bed).
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the precise technique for making a hospital corner. - Explain and demonstrate turn-down service. - Show how to prepare an extra bed or cot.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of hospital corner technique. - Trainer observation of turn-down service setup.
topics.resources: - Bed with various bed linen. - Dummy for occupied bed practice. - Extra bed/cot if available.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Apply basic decorative elements to guest beds. - Understand the impact of bed presentation on guest experience.
topics.activities: - Showcase different ways to decorate guest beds (e.g., throw pillows, folded blankets, chocolates). - Discuss the aesthetic appeal and attention to detail. - Provide examples of creative bed presentation.
topics.assessment: - Group discussion on bed presentation. - Short design activity: "Decorate this bed" with provided items.
topics.resources: - Decorative pillows, throws, small amenity items. - Pictures of creatively decorated hotel beds.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Make a guest bed efficiently and to high standards. - Ensure all bed making procedures are followed.
topics.activities: - Supervise trainees in making full guest beds, incorporating all learned techniques. - Provide individual feedback and correction. - Simulate guest room scenarios.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees make a guest bed to industry standards within a time limit (Summative for LO2). - Third-party report (if applicable, e.g., from a practicing hotelier).
topics.resources: - Fully equipped mock guest rooms. - Sufficient supply of clean and fresh linen. - Bed making checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Identify and describe different laundry equipment. - Categorize various laundry chemicals and supplies.
topics.activities: - Lecture on types of washing machines, dryers, and ironing equipment. - Display and explain various laundry detergents, softeners, and stain removers. - Discuss the functions of each material.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on laundry equipment functions. - Short written quiz on laundry chemical types.
topics.resources: - Pictures/diagrams of commercial laundry equipment. - Laundry chemical labels (empty containers). - Safety data sheets for laundry chemicals.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Sort laundry based on fabric type, color, and degree of soiling. - Inspect articles for damage, stains, and personal items.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate proper laundry sorting techniques. - Guide trainees on inspecting garments for damages, missing buttons, and personal items. - Emphasize pre-treatment of stains.
topics.assessment: - Practical sorting exercise (formative). - Observation of garment inspection.
topics.resources: - Assortment of laundry items (various fabrics, colors). - Stain pre-treatment products. - Inspection checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Operate a washing machine effectively. - Apply appropriate washing cycles for different fabrics.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the safe and correct operation of a washing machine. - Explain different wash cycles (e.g., delicate, heavy duty, normal). - Supervise hands-on practice.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of washing machine operation (formative). - Oral questioning on wash cycle selection.
topics.resources: - Working washing machine (if available, otherwise simulation). - Various fabric samples with care labels. - Laundry instructions/manuals.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Operate a dryer effectively. - Fold different laundry articles neatly.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the safe and correct operation of a dryer. - Guide trainees on proper folding techniques for various items (towels, sheets, shirts). - Discuss the importance of prompt drying and folding.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of dryer operation (formative). - Observation of folding techniques.
topics.resources: - Working dryer (if available, otherwise simulation). - Assortment of clean, dry laundry items for folding. - Folding guides/diagrams.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Understand the purpose of laundry checklists. - Create a basic laundry process checklist.
topics.activities: - Lecture on the importance of checklists in laundry operations. - Provide examples of different laundry checklists (e.g., for sorting, washing, finishing). - Facilitate a group activity to design a checklist.
topics.assessment: - Group presentation and critique of designed checklists. - Oral questioning on the purpose of laundry checklists.
topics.resources: - Sample laundry checklists. - Flip charts/whiteboard for group work.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Perform the complete laundry process for towels and bed linens. - Adhere to hygiene and quality standards.
topics.activities: - Supervise trainees in sorting, washing, drying, and folding a batch of towels and bed linens. - Provide feedback on efficiency and quality. - Emphasize infection control measures.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees perform a complete laundry cycle for towels/linens (formative for LO3). - Trainer observation of adherence to checklist.
topics.resources: - Batch of soiled towels and bed linens. - Full laundry facility (or simulation with relevant equipment). - Laundry detergents and softeners.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Identify different types of ironing and pressing equipment. - Explain the functions of each finishing tool.
topics.activities: - Lecture on steam irons, ironing boards, garment steamers, and presses. - Demonstrate the safe setup and operation of each equipment. - Discuss heat settings for various fabrics.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on finishing equipment functions. - Short written quiz on heat settings.
topics.resources: - Various ironing/pressing equipment (if available, otherwise visuals). - Heat setting guides for fabrics.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · -Prepare different articles for ironing or pressing. - Understand appropriate temperature settings for various fabrics.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate pre-ironing preparation (e.g., dampening, turning garments inside out). - Guide trainees on identifying fabric types and their corresponding heat requirements.
topics.assessment: - Practical sorting and preparation exercise. - Oral questioning on care label interpretation.
topics.resources: - Assortment of clean, dry garments (shirts, trousers, dresses). - Spray bottle for dampening. - Fabric care label guide.

topics.learningOutcomes: - Iron shirts, trousers, and flat linen effectively. - Maintain safety during ironing.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the systematic approach to ironing shirts, trousers, and flat linen. - Emphasize safety precautions (e.g., cord management, heat control). - Provide hands-on guided practice.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of ironing techniques (formative). - Trainer observation of safety practices.
topics.resources: - Irons, ironing boards. - Various clean, unironed garments and flat linen. - Instructional videos on ironing techniques.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · - Use a garment steamer effectively. - Operate a pressing machine (if available) safely.
topics.activities: - Demonstrate the correct use of a garment steamer for delicate fabrics. - (If available) Demonstrate the operation of a professional pressing machine. - Discuss when to use steaming versus ironing.
topics.assessment: - Practical demonstration of steaming (formative). - Oral questioning on choice of finishing method.
topics.resources: - Garment steamer. - (If available) Pressing machine. - Delicate garments (e.g., silk, rayon).

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · -Understand the purpose of finishing checklists. - Create a basic finishing checklist.
topics.activities: - Lecture on the importance of checklists in the finishing process. - Provide examples of different finishing checklists. - Facilitate a group activity to design a checklist.
topics.assessment: - Group presentation and critique of designed checklists. - Oral questioning on the purpose of finishing checklists.
topics.resources: - Sample finishing checklists. - Flip charts/whiteboard for group work.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · -Finish a variety of articles to a professional standard. - Package finished articles appropriately.
topics.activities: - Supervise trainees in ironing, steaming, and folding a diverse range of articles. - Provide feedback on quality and presentation. - Demonstrate proper folding for storage and packaging.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees iron/finish a selection of items to professional standards (formative for LO3). - Trainer observation of packaging quality.
topics.resources: - Assortment of clean, unironed garments (shirts, dresses, table linen). - Irons, steamers, ironing boards. - Hangers, garment bags, folding boards.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to --Perform cleaning and bed making in a simulated guest room environment. - Manage time effectively to complete tasks.
topics.activities: - Set up a simulated guest room scenario (e.g., check-out room). - Provide a checklist for the full room cleaning and bed making. - Observe and provide feedback on the complete process.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees perform integrated room cleaning and bed making (Summative for LO1 & LO2). - Use of a comprehensive rubric.
topics.resources: - Fully equipped mock guest room. - Cleaning equipment, materials, and fresh linen. - Integrated room cleaning checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · -Understand the importance of quality control in housekeeping. - Identify common quality issues in cleaning, bed making, and laundry.
topics.activities: - Lecture on quality standards in housekeeping. - Discuss common deficiencies and how to prevent them. - Introduce the concept of guest satisfaction and feedback.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on quality standards. - Group activity: "Spot the errors" in simulated scenarios.
topics.resources: - Quality standard documents (e.g., hotel brand standards). - Examples of poor cleaning/bed making (pictures). - Guest feedback forms (samples).

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to --Perform the complete laundry process for various articles efficiently. - Ensure high quality in washing and finishing.
topics.activities: - Set up a simulated laundry batch with diverse articles. - Provide a comprehensive laundry and finishing checklist. - Observe and provide feedback on the entire laundry process.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees perform an integrated laundry and finishing cycle (Summative for LO3). - Trainer observation and completion of rubric.
topics.resources: - Assorted soiled and unironed laundry items. - Full laundry facility (or simulation). - Comprehensive laundry and finishing checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to - - identify common hazards in housekeeping. - Apply safety procedures to prevent accidents. - Use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) correctly.
topics.activities: - Lecture on common OSH hazards (slips, trips, falls, chemical exposure, ergonomic risks). - Demonstrate the correct use of various PPE (gloves, masks, eye protection). - Conduct a safety walk-through of the training area.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on OSH hazards and prevention. - Practical demonstration of PPE use.
topics.resources: - OSH Act (Kenya) excerpts. - Various PPE samples. - Hazard identification checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to · -Apply ergonomic principles to housekeeping tasks. - Demonstrate safe manual handling techniques.
topics.activities: - Lecture on ergonomic principles in lifting, pushing, and pulling. - Demonstrate safe manual handling techniques (e.g., lifting heavy objects, moving trolleys). - Provide hands-on practice with various objects.

topics.topic: Introduction to Nutrition Education and Counselling
topics.coverage:  Meaning of terms: nutrition education, counsellor, nutrition counselling ·  Origin and evolution of the field ·  Modern practices in nutrition: dietary guidelines, nutrition science, roles of professionals, public health initiatives ·  Objectives of nutrition education and counselling: healthy eating habits, improved dietary behaviors, empowerment, disease prevention ·  Principles of nutrition education: learner-centered, evidence-based, interactive, positive, culturally sensitive ·  Principles of nutrition counselling: client-centered, collaborative partnership, motivational interviewing, small changes, holistic approach

 Meaning of healthy human behavior ·  Factors influencing behavior: personal, social, environmental, psychological ·  Health and nutrition education models and theories: Health Belief Model (HBM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), Social Cognitive Theory, Transtheoretical Model (Stages of Change Model), Social Ecological Model

topics.topic: Communication in Nutrition Education and Counselling
topics.coverage:  Importance of communication in nutrition education and counselling ·  Components of communication: sender, message, channel, receiver, feedback ·  Characteristics of a good educator/counsellor: communication skills, credibility, empathy, motivational interviewing, positive, knowledgeable, empathetic listener, non-judgmental, flexible ·  Methods of teaching and materials: lectures, discussions, demonstrations, activities, visual aids, printed materials, technology ·  Developing educational messages for individuals and groups: audience-specific, focus on benefits, clear language, realistic goals, motivational

 Aims of nutrition counselling: improved dietary behaviors, empowerment, healthy eating habits, behavior change, specific health conditions ·  Steps in nutrition counselling: assessment, diagnosis, goal setting, education, intervention, evaluation & follow-up ·  Counselling in multicultural settings: cultural sensitivity, dietary restrictions, language barriers, cultural influences on behavior change ·  Techniques in counselling: motivational interviewing, behavior change strategies, building rapport ·  Roles and qualities of a nutrition counsellor: educator, motivational coach, counsellor, advocate ·  Vulnerable groups and the need for counselling: children, pregnant/lactating women, older adults, low-income individuals, chronic health conditions

- Focus on Pregnancy and Pediatric Needs · Pregnancy: aims, counselling points (e.g., folic acid, balanced diet, food safety, managing cravings/nausea) · Pediatrics: aims, counselling points (e.g., age-specific nutrients, variety of foods, picky eaters, introducing new foods, allergies)

 Adolescence: aims, counselling points (e.g., bone health, body image, healthy snacking, communication) ·  Geriatrics: aims, counselling points (e.g., muscle mass, digestion, food insecurity, chronic diseases)

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to --Perform cleaning and bed making in a simulated guest room environment. - Manage time effectively to complete tasks.
topics.activities: - Set up a simulated guest room scenario (e.g., check-out room). - Provide a checklist for the full room cleaning and bed making. - Observe and provide feedback on the complete process.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees perform integrated room cleaning and bed making (Summative for LO1 & LO2). - Use of a comprehensive rubric.
topics.resources: - Fully equipped mock guest room. - Cleaning equipment, materials, and fresh linen. - Integrated room cleaning checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to: · -Understand the importance of quality control in housekeeping. - Identify common quality issues in cleaning, bed making, and laundry.
topics.activities: - Lecture on quality standards in housekeeping. - Discuss common deficiencies and how to prevent them. - Introduce the concept of guest satisfaction and feedback.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on quality standards. - Group activity: "Spot the errors" in simulated scenarios.
topics.resources: - Quality standard documents (e.g., hotel brand standards). - Examples of poor cleaning/bed making (pictures). - Guest feedback forms (samples).

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to --Perform the complete laundry process for various articles efficiently. - Ensure high quality in washing and finishing.
topics.activities: - Set up a simulated laundry batch with diverse articles. - Provide a comprehensive laundry and finishing checklist. - Observe and provide feedback on the entire laundry process.
topics.assessment: - Practical Assessment: Trainees perform an integrated laundry and finishing cycle (Summative for LO3). - Trainer observation and completion of rubric.
topics.resources: - Assorted soiled and unironed laundry items. - Full laundry facility (or simulation). - Comprehensive laundry and finishing checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to - - identify common hazards in housekeeping. - Apply safety procedures to prevent accidents. - Use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) correctly.
topics.activities: - Lecture on common OSH hazards (slips, trips, falls, chemical exposure, ergonomic risks). - Demonstrate the correct use of various PPE (gloves, masks, eye protection). - Conduct a safety walk-through of the training area.
topics.assessment: - Oral questioning on OSH hazards and prevention. - Practical demonstration of PPE use.
topics.resources: - OSH Act (Kenya) excerpts. - Various PPE samples. - Hazard identification checklist.

topics.learningOutcomes: By the end of the session trainee should be able to · -Apply ergonomic principles to housekeeping tasks. - Demonstrate safe manual handling techniques.
topics.activities: - Lecture on ergonomic principles in lifting, pushing, and pulling. - Demonstrate safe manual handling techniques (e.g., lifting heavy objects, moving trolleys). - Provide hands-on practice with various objects.

extraction.unitDescription: This module unit is intended to equip the trainee with knowledge, skills, and attitudes in the development, marketing, and sales of industrial products. Emphasis is placed on the product development process, prototype testing, commercialization, marketing management, and sales evaluation, enabling learners to apply these skills in real-life industrial and community nutrition contexts. General Objectives General Objectives By the end of this course, the student should be able to:1. Describe the stages in product development from idea generation to commercialization.2. Apply skills in planning and commercialization of new products.3. Market new products effectively.4. Evaluate product sales and adapt to emerging market challenges.
extraction.learningOutcomes: SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (COMPETENCIES) At the end of the course, the trainee should be able to: Explain the meaning, importance, and life cycle of product development. Identify and process ideas into viable product concepts. Produce and evaluate prototypes for commercial viability. Analyze factors affecting new product success and apply quality control measures. Conduct market sampling, product trials, and customer feedback evaluation. Develop and implement product commercialization plans. Apply principles of marketing management, marketing mix, and entry strategies. Demonstrate salesmanship, sales process, and sales management skills.
extraction.references: REFERENCES / RECOMMENDED READING 1. Kotler, P., & Armstrong, G. (2017). Principles of Marketing (17th Ed.). Pearson.2. Lamb, C. W., Hair, J. F., & McDaniel, C. (2018). Marketing (13th Ed.). Cengage.3. Trott, P. (2017). Innovation Management and New Product Development (6th Ed.). Pearson.4. Kerin, R., Hartley, S., & Rudelius, W. (2015). Marketing: The Core (6th Ed.). McGraw-Hill.5. Kotler, P., & Keller, K. L. (2016). Marketing Management (15th Ed.). Pearson. extraction.unitDescription: This module is designed to equip trainees with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to understand and apply epidemiological principles in the context of nutrition and dietetics. It covers the determinants and distribution of nutrition-related diseases in populations, methods of epidemiological investigation, and the application of epidemiology in planning, implementing, and evaluating community nutrition and health services. 4. COURSE OBJECTIVES By the end of the module unit, the trainee should be able to: • Appreciate the role of nutrition epidemiology in nutrition and dietetics. • Apply nutrition epidemiology principles in nutrition and dietetics. • Understand how to conduct epidemiologic studies in nutrition and dietetics. • Develop a positive attitude towards planning and evaluating community nutrition services. • Appreciate the role of effective record keeping in epidemiologic studies in nutrition and dietetics.
extraction.learningOutcomes: By the end of the module unit, the trainee should be able to: • Appreciate the importance of epidemiology. • Analyse the epidemiological triad of disease. • Identify areas where nutritional epidemiology is applied. • Apply knowledge and skills in determining morbidity, mortality and fertility rates of a population. • Apply skills in epidemiology in disease prevention. • Establish a population screening programme. • Investigate an outbreak. • Select an appropriate method for epidemiological study of a disease. • Apply knowledge in planning and evaluating community health services.

It gives a broad knowledge of raw food materials and their application in meal management. COURSE OBJECTIVES By the end of the module unit, the trainee should be able to: Appreciate the role of nutrition epidemiology in nutrition and dietetics. Apply nutrition epidemiology principles in nutrition and dietetics. Understand how to conduct epidemiologic studies in nutrition and dietetics. Develop a positive attitude towards planning and evaluating community nutrition services. Appreciate the role of effective record keeping in epidemiologic studies in nutrition and dietetics.
extraction.learningOutcomes: By the end of the module unit, the trainee should be able to: Appreciate the importance of epidemiology. Analyze the epidemiological triad of disease. Identify areas where nutritional epidemiology is applied. Have the ability to apply knowledge and skills in determining morbidity, mortality and fertility rates of a population. Apply skills in epidemiology in disease prevention. Establish population screening programme. Investigate an outbreak. Select an appropriate method for epidemiological study of a disease. Apply knowledge learnt in planning and evaluating community health services.
